Last week I flew to ACC Headquarters for the ACC SAAC meetings; a chance to sit down with fellow student-athletes and leadership from across the conference to talk through where college athletics stands right now. One of the most tangible outcomes: we drafted letters supporting the Protect College Sports Act (PCSA) and sent them to our senators, pushing to get it in front of the Senate before the August recess. It's not a perfect bill and it's still being negotiated, but it's one of the few real efforts in Congress right now to bring some stability to a system that badly needs it. Grateful for the chance to represent Stanford's student-athlete body in these conversations with the Commissioner, and to hear directly from peers across the conference about what they're seeing on their own campuses. ...more ...more

Human Archive (YC W26) builds datasets to model sensorimotor intelligence for robotics and world models. HA-Multi is the largest dataset of manual labor tasks aligning egocentric RGB, stereo depth (IR dot projection), tactile gloves, body IMUs, and wrist cameras. Human intelligence is predominantly embodied, and the internet does not capture it. Every day we perceive the world, apply force, and adapt to noisy real-world environments. Yet no dataset captures this multimodal structure of human interaction with the world at scale. As a result, progress in embodied spatial intelligence has been bottlenecked. To collect data at scale and ensure quality, they build and deploy custom hardware across homes and businesses, then post-process the resulting data through internal QA, anonymization, annotation pipelines, and policy benchmarking. They've already shipped data to frontier research teams and will open-source samples next week. If you’re interested, reach out: raj@humanarchive.ai Congrats on the launch, Shloke Patel , Samay Maini , Rushil Agarwal and Raj Patel ! 🚀 https://lnkd.in/g3HqFukn ...more ...more

K BBQ with a bunch of people who are building their own thing in one way or another. Nobody here has it “figured out.” We’re just trying. Learning. Messing up. Fixing it. Trying again. Talking about ideas that might work. Laughing about the ones that definitely won’t. NYC makes this normal. You go out for dinner and suddenly you’re talking about apps, jobs, goals, life direction, money, purpose, all in the span of 20 minutes. And it doesn’t feel heavy. It just feels exciting. This is the part of the journey I actually love. The late night food. The side quests. The people you collect along the way. Tired of Claude outputting overly verbose jargon filled slop? Try this simple prompt: "Set Claude Code output style to Simplified Technical English ASD-STE100" This will configure Claude to speak Simplified Technical English, greatly increasing the legibility of the output. Especially needed with the newest Fable 5 and Opus 5 models, they dive into jargon so quickly, sometimes they even invent their own jargon during thinking and output it to the user.
